issue.title: [PUL-182] feat(server): TTL cleanup for stale issue_skill_state rows
issue.body:
multica: [PUL-182](https://multica.ai/issues/PUL-182)

## Summary

PUL-177 ([#36](https://github.com/rabbeet/multica/pull/36)) shipped `issue_skill_state` with a two-state machine (`in_progress` → `done`). A skill that started but never reported `done` — claude-code crashed, rate-limit hit, agent worktree force-killed, user Ctrl-C — leaves a phantom `in_progress` chip in the Inbox forever. (The agent-1 rate-limit leak comment on the parent multica issue is itself an example of the failure shape.)

This PR is the cron half of the fix called out in PUL-177's plan "Failure modes" D7: a TTL sweep that deletes stale `in_progress` rows every 15 minutes (default 24h TTL, override via `ISSUE_SKILL_STATE_STALE_TTL`). `done` rows are intentionally never touched — they back LastSkillChip + SkillHistory and must persist.

## Plan

This PR implements [`2026-05-18-pul-182-issue-skill-state-ttl-cleanup.md`](https://github.com/rabbeet/plans/blob/main/Multica/2026-05-18-pul-182-issue-skill-state-ttl-cleanup.md). Published before implementation started (audit log).

Three options were on the table (Mechanism A/B/C from [PUL-182](https://multica.ai/issues/PUL-182) description). Chose **A (cron + DELETE)**:

- vs B (lazy filter on read) — leaves rows in the DB, splits behavior between Inbox and Issue-detail pages, accumulates dead state.
- vs C (new `stale` enum) — needs a migration to extend `CHECK (status IN ('in_progress', 'done'))`, plus new UI styling. Over-engineering for v1.1.

## Changes

- `server/pkg/db/queries/issue_skill_state.sql` — new `CleanupStaleIssueSkillStates :many` query. Uses `make_interval(secs => @ttl_seconds::bigint)` for typed-int TTL; `status = 'in_progress'` strict (so a future `stale` enum is an explicit re-decision); `RETURNING` shapes per-row debug logs without a follow-up SELECT.
- `server/pkg/db/generated/issue_skill_state.sql.go` — regenerated via `sqlc generate` (v1.31.1).
- `server/internal/handler/skill_state_cleanup_test.go` — 5 query-level cases: stale `in_progress` deleted; fresh `in_progress` preserved; `done` never touched (even at 100d age); 4-row mixed batch; strict-`<` TTL boundary.
- `server/cmd/server/skill_state_cleanup_scheduler.go` — `runSkillStateCleanupScheduler` on a 15-min ticker. Synchronous startup tick so post-crash recovery is not stuck waiting 15 minutes. `slog.Info` only fires when something was actually cleaned (silent on healthy idle); `slog.Debug` per row for ops debugging.
- `server/cmd/server/skill_state_cleanup_scheduler_test.go` — 3 tick-level cases: stale row deleted by tick; fresh + done preserved; cancelled-context tick returns without panic.
- `server/cmd/server/main.go` — one `envDuration("ISSUE_SKILL_STATE_STALE_TTL", 24*time.Hour)` + one `go runSkillStateCleanupScheduler(...)` slotted next to the other `autopilotCtx`-scoped schedulers (shares graceful-shutdown contract).

No migration. No frontend change. CHECK constraint untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` clean
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test ./...` — non-DB tests pass; DB-dependent tests skip via the existing `TestMain` `pool.Ping → os.Exit(0)` path on this brainstorm host (no local PG with `multica:multica` superuser). CI runs them against the docker-up postgres service (see `.github/workflows/ci.yml`).
- [ ] CI green on Go test suite (this PR + new tests)
- [ ] Manual: deploy to staging, set `ISSUE_SKILL_STATE_STALE_TTL=1m`, verify scheduler log line `skill_state cleanup: removed stale in_progress rows deleted=N ttl=1m0s` appears once and stays quiet thereafter.

## Agent context

Built by `agent-2` running as a multica.ai workspace agent on the host (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/home/multica/.claude/agent-2/`, worktree=`/srv/agent-worktrees/agent-2-pul-182-skill-state-ttl-cleanup/`). Plan + implementation in one session. Worktree branch: `agent-2/pul-182-skill-state-ttl-cleanup`. Spawned after agent-1 hit a claude.ai rate-limit on the same task (the leaked rate-limit string is preserved as the first comment on [PUL-182](https://multica.ai/issues/PUL-182) for context — not deleted).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

issue.title: [PUL-148] fix(cascade): adapter relaxation + issue-based loop guard
issue.body:
multica: [PUL-148](https://multica.ai/issues/PUL-148)

## Summary

Unsticks the PUL-102 cascade pipeline on real GitHub deliveries. Verified empirically on the [PUL-143](https://multica.ai/issues/PUL-143) smoke 2026-05-16: webhook arrived (App Recent Deliveries 2xx), but no `cascade_retrigger` row was ever persisted because the adapter rejected `workflow_run.pull_requests=[]` payloads — the legitimate same-repo PR case.

Two coupled fixes:

### 1. Adapter relaxation (`server/internal/webhooks/github/source.go`)

`normalizeWorkflowRun` and `normalizeCheckRun` previously required `len(pull_requests) == 1`. GitHub frequently ships `pull_requests=[]` for legitimate same-repo PR runs (verified via `gh api repos/.../actions/runs/<id>` — count: 0 PRs on a run unambiguously tied to PR #498).

Fix: accept `len == 0` (persist with `PRURL=""` `PRNumber=0`; worker resolves issue from `Branch` via existing `LookupIssueIdentifier`). Keep `len > 1` skip — genuine ambiguity from forks / merge queues.

### 2. Loop-guard rekey (`server/internal/cascade/worker.go`)

`checkLoopGuard` keyed off `pr_url`. With the adapter relaxation, multiple events with `pr_url=""` would collapse into one bucket and false-trip after 3 distinct head_shas across unrelated PRs.

Fix: key the loop guard on `issue_id` (already populated by `resolveIssue` before this check runs). Threshold unchanged (3 distinct head_shas in 6h). Semantically tighter for multi-PR-per-issue agents.

### 3. Index (`server/migrations/076_*`)

New `idx_cascade_retrigger_loop_guard_by_issue (issue_id, action, fired_at DESC)` serving the new query shape. Old `idx_cascade_retrigger_loop_guard (pr_url, ...)` left in place — analytics queries still benefit from it; dropping it is a separate cleanup.

### 4. Contract amendment (`server/internal/webhooks/event.go`)

`TriggerEvent` docstring updated: `PRURL`/`PRNumber` may be zero when `HeadSHA` + `Branch` carry enough for the worker to resolve the issue (PUL-148 case).

### 5. Tests (`source_test.go`)

Explicit fixtures for the empty-`pull_requests` path on both `workflow_run` and `check_run`.

## Trade-offs vs the originally-proposed Option A

The PUL-148 description proposed a worker-side `commits/{sha}/pulls` API call to back-fill `pr_url`. That would have introduced GitHub credentials in the worker (breaking source-agnostic design) and added latency. The issue-based loop guard achieves the same correctness with no new external dependency and a more protective semantic (per-issue rather than per-PR).

`PRURL`/`PRNumber` in the agent `TriggerContext` will be empty for `workflow_run`/`check_run` events with `pull_requests=[]`. Agents that need the PR url can `gh pr list --head <head_sha>` themselves; this matches the existing behaviour after the worker drains pending events (the agent context already runs in a worktree with `gh` available).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI on this PR passes
- [ ] After merge: open a new failing-test PR on rabbeet/Pulse, expect the cascade comment in the source ticket within ~30s of `workflow_run.completed`
- [ ] Loop guard still trips on the existing scenario (3 distinct head_shas same issue 6h)
- [ ] Once smoke confirms, [PUL-143](https://multica.ai/issues/PUL-143) can be flipped from `waiting` → `deployed`

comment.body:
Closing as redundant — PR #21 (`fix/cascade-github-empty-pulls-fallback`) already shipped a fix for the same root cause via the worker-side `commits/{sha}/pulls` API lookup (the original Option A from PUL-148 description). Merged 2026-05-17T06:20:02Z, deployed.

I missed it because the multica-bare.git mirror on this host hadn't fetched the new main pointer when I started. Closing this branch rather than rebasing.

My branch contained one orthogonal improvement worth following up separately if it ever bites: `checkLoopGuard` keyed on `pr_url` could still produce false positives when an issue accumulates 3+ distinct head_shas across multiple PRs in the 6h window. Issue-based loop guard would tighten that — opening as a follow-up if I see it manifest.
